entities.summary: Andrea Navagero, known as Andreas Naugerius in Latin, was a Venetian diplomat and writer. Born to a wealthy family, he gained entry to the Great Council of Venice at the age of twenty, five years younger than was normal at the time. He dedicated himself to editing classical Latin manuscripts at the Aldine Press printing office, garnering a reputation as a scholar and a skilled writer. In 1515, at the request of the general Bartolomeo d'Alviano, he was appointed the caretaker of a library containing the collection of the scholar Bessarion; this library would later become the Biblioteca Marciana.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Andrea Navagero's appointment as caretaker of Bessarion's library in 1515 led to the preservation and dissemination of classical Latin manuscripts, contributing to the growth of human knowledge during the Renaissance. His work at the Aldine Press further solidified his reputation as a scholar and writer.
